claims.text: HEA resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion is primarily governed by formation of a robust, self-healing, multi-component passive film.
The passive film is enriched in corrosion-resistant elements that are uniformly distributed throughout the HEA.
The passive film rapidly reforms after mechanical removal.
Rapid passive-film reformation limits both mechanical material loss and chemical attack.
Casting followed by thermomechanical processing can produce the proposed HEA with a near-homogeneous microstructure and uniform elemental distribution.
The proposed baseline has fewer alloying elements, lower configurational entropy, and less passivation-promoting solute than the HEA.
The protective oxide is enriched in passivation-promoting elements such as Cr or Al.
High configurational entropy drives a uniform passive-film presence across the HEA surface.
High configurational entropy enables a uniform elemental distribution.
Uniform elemental distribution promotes rapid formation and continuous self-healing of the protective oxide.
The protective film minimizes the active surface area exposed to the corrosive electrolyte.
The protective film reduces friction and mechanical material removal.
Combined degradation is controlled by the dynamic balance between mechanical film erosion and film regeneration.
Under matched test conditions, the HEA will have a lower wear-track depth than the baseline.
Under matched test conditions, the HEA will have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline.
Under matched test conditions, the HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
The HEA will synergistically mitigate both wear and corrosion relative to the corresponding separate degradation phenomena in the baseline.
The predicted advantage should hold when passive-film formation is not limited by extremely high wear rates or surface contamination.
The HEA advantage may disappear when mechanical removal exceeds film-reformation kinetics.
Defects, impurities, and processing-induced heterogeneity can inhibit uniform oxide formation and reduce degradation resistance.
